title: A Blockchain-Based Approach to Provenance and Reproducibility in Research Workflows
authors: Kevin Wittek, Iryna Dohndorf, Neslihan Wittek, Alexander Weinert, James Lawton, Andrei Ionita
conference: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Big Data
hypotheses: Blockchain technology can enable new certification models that capture research processes holistically, addressing reproducibility crisis through immutable provenance tracking
notes: Introduces blockchain service for research data certification using cryptographic fingerprinting. Uses bloxberg scientific blockchain infrastructure with deep learning behavioral science case study
strengths: Addresses fundamental reproducibility crisis, provides concrete technical implementation, demonstrates real-world application
weaknesses: Limited to specific use cases, potential scalability concerns for large datasets, requires significant infrastructure changes
citation: Wittek et al., A Blockchain-Based Approach to Provenance and Reproducibility in Research Workflows, IEEE Big Data 2021

title: SciChain: Blockchain-enabled Lightweight and Efficient Data Provenance for Reproducible Scientific Computing
authors: Abdullah Al-Mamun, Feng Yan, Dongfang Zhao
conference: 37th IEEE International Conference on Data Engineering (ICDE)
hypotheses: Proof-of-scalable-traceability (POST) protocol can deliver trustworthy data provenance services on HPC systems with minimal overhead
notes: First practical blockchain system for provenance services on HPC. Introduces POST consensus protocol specifically designed for scientific applications
strengths: Orders of magnitude lower overhead than existing solutions, specifically designed for HPC environments, novel consensus mechanism
weaknesses: Limited to HPC contexts, new and untested consensus mechanism, potential adoption barriers
citation: Al-Mamun et al., SciChain: Blockchain-enabled Lightweight and Efficient Data Provenance for Reproducible Scientific Computing, ICDE 2021

title: Introducing the Open Science Chain - Protecting Integrity and Provenance of Research Data
authors: Subhashini Sivagnanam, Viswanath Nandigam, Kai Lin
hypotheses: Blockchain cyberinfrastructure can address reproducibility and accountability issues in scientific research through secure metadata storage and auditable change tracking
notes: NSF-funded Open Science Chain platform using blockchain for research data metadata verification. Addresses data withholding and misrepresentation concerns
strengths: NSF funding demonstrates institutional support, focuses on practical researcher incentives, addresses real barriers to data sharing
weaknesses: Early stage project, limited deployment data, potential integration challenges with existing workflows
citation: Sivagnanam et al., Introducing the Open Science Chain - Protecting Integrity and Provenance of Research Data, NSF 2019

title: The Verification of Ecological Citizen Science Data: Current Approaches and Future Possibilities
authors: E.R. Baker, J.P. Drury, J. Judge, D.B. Roy, G.C. Smith, P.A. Stephens
hypotheses: Expert verification, community consensus, and automated approaches each have distinct advantages for different types of citizen science data verification
notes: Systematic review of 259 citizen science schemes examining verification approaches. Expert verification most widely used, community consensus and automated systems emerging
strengths: Comprehensive systematic review, large sample size, practical focus on implementation approaches
weaknesses: Limited to ecological citizen science, may not generalize to other domains, traditional focus without blockchain integration
citation: Baker et al., The Verification of Ecological Citizen Science Data: Current Approaches and Future Possibilities, Durham 2025

title: Perspectives on Citizen Science Data Quality
authors: Robert R. Downs, Hampapuram K. Ramapriyan, Ge Peng, Yaxing Wei
hypotheses: Quality assessment and quality control frameworks can improve citizen science data trustworthiness and enable broader data reuse
notes: Comprehensive review of QA/QC issues for citizen science data, offering perspectives on quality improvement and research methodologies
strengths: Focuses on practical quality improvement strategies, addresses data reuse opportunities, comprehensive quality framework
weaknesses: Traditional QA/QC approaches, limited discussion of decentralized validation mechanisms, no blockchain integration
citation: Downs et al., Perspectives on Citizen Science Data Quality, Frontiers in Climate 2021

title: A Sensor Network Approach to Managing Data Quality in Citizen Science
authors: Andrea Wiggins, Carl Lagoze, Weng-Keen Wong, Steve Kelling
conference: AAAI Conference on Human Computation and Crowdsourcing
hypotheses: Sensor network strategies can be adapted for managing citizen science data quality when traditional ground truth comparison is not possible
notes: Presents eBird case study using autonomous sensor network approaches for human sensor quality assessment in bird identification tasks
strengths: Novel adaptation of sensor network principles to human sensing, real-world case study with eBird, addresses fundamental quality challenge
weaknesses: Limited to biological observation domains, requires large user base for effectiveness, traditional centralized approach
citation: Wiggins et al., A Sensor Network Approach to Managing Data Quality in Citizen Science, AAAI HCOMP 2014

title: Validation of Citizen Science Meteorological Data: Can They Be Considered a Valid Help in Weather Understanding and Community Engagement?
authors: Nicola Loglisci, Massimo Milelli, Juri Iurato, Timoteo Galia, Antonella Galizia, Antonio Parodi
hypotheses: Citizen science meteorological data can achieve high quality and reliability when properly validated against official weather networks
notes: MeteoTracker I-CHANGE project validation study comparing citizen science measurements with official Italian civil protection weather network. Demonstrates high correlation and reliability
strengths: Rigorous validation methodology, large-scale real-world dataset, demonstrates practical utility of citizen science data
weaknesses: Limited to meteorological data, requires official network for validation, traditional centralized validation approach
citation: Loglisci et al., Validation of Citizen Science Meteorological Data, Sensors 2024

title: Designing a Token Economy: Incentives, Governance, and Tokenomics
authors: Samela Kivilo, Alex Norta, Marie Hattingh, Sowelu Avanzo
hypotheses: Step-by-step token economy design model can effectively integrate incentives, governance, and tokenomics for diverse applications
notes: Proposes holistic design science research methodology for token economies. Evaluated using Currynomics case study with real estate-backed stablecoin
strengths: Comprehensive design framework, practical case study validation, addresses key tokenomics dimensions systematically
weaknesses: Limited to specific use case validation, complex implementation requirements, potential scalability questions
citation: Kivilo et al., Designing a Token Economy: Incentives, Governance, and Tokenomics, Blockchain R&A 2025

title: Tokenomics and Incentive Mechanisms: Driving User Engagement and Liquidity in DeFi Platforms
authors: Lee Micheal
hypotheses: Strategic tokenomics design significantly influences user behavior, platform growth, and capital inflow in DeFi protocols
notes: Mixed-methods analysis of tokenomics strategies across DeFi protocols examining impact on user engagement and liquidity sustainability
strengths: Quantitative metrics from real platform data, comprehensive categorization of tokenomics strategies, practical insights for platform design
weaknesses: Limited to DeFi context, may not directly apply to research contexts, potential market volatility effects on conclusions
citation: Micheal, Tokenomics and Incentive Mechanisms: Driving User Engagement and Liquidity in DeFi Platforms, ResearchGate 2022

title: Blockchain for local communities: an exploratory review of token economy aspects
authors: Irene Domenicale, Cristina Viano, Claudio Schifanella
hypotheses: Blockchain applications for local communities require different tokenization mechanisms than mainstream cryptocurrencies to support collaborative and social purposes
notes: Exploratory review of token economy elements in blockchain applications for local community economies, examining socio-economic value transactions
strengths: Focus on community-oriented applications, examination of social vs economic motivations, practical case studies
weaknesses: Limited to local community context, exploratory rather than empirical, potential scalability questions for larger research communities
citation: Domenicale et al., Blockchain for local communities: an exploratory review of token economy aspects, Front. Blockchain 2024

title: Non-algorithmic governance mechanisms of blockchain-based decentralized autonomous organizations
authors: C. Andriopoulos, M.W. Lewis
hypotheses: Non-algorithmic governance mechanisms are essential complements to smart contracts in DAO operations and decision-making processes
notes: Examination of governance mechanisms beyond smart contracts in blockchain-based DAOs, focusing on human elements in decentralized governance
strengths: Addresses practical governance challenges, human-centered approach to DAO design, empirical methodology
weaknesses: May not fully address scientific research contexts, limited technical implementation details, potential generalizability issues
citation: Andriopoulos & Lewis, Non-algorithmic governance mechanisms of blockchain-based decentralized autonomous organizations, Technovation 2025

title: Blockchain-based governance models supporting corruption detection and prevention
authors: D. Mourtzis, J. Angelopoulos, N. Panopoulos
hypotheses: Blockchain-based governance models with self-sovereign identity can effectively detect and prevent corruption while maintaining user privacy
notes: Focuses on Web3.0 and self-sovereign identity for transparent governance, emphasizing corruption prevention through decentralized systems
strengths: Addresses critical governance challenges, practical corruption detection mechanisms, privacy-preserving approaches
weaknesses: Limited to corruption detection context, may not address scientific research governance needs specifically, implementation complexity
citation: Mourtzis et al., Blockchain-based governance models supporting corruption detection and prevention, Blockchain R&A 2024

title: Blockchain Revolutionizing Healthcare Industry: A Systematic Review of Blockchain Technology Benefits and Threats
authors: Fatma M AbdelSalam
hypotheses: Blockchain technology can address healthcare industry challenges related to data security, interoperability, and patient privacy while introducing new operational complexities
notes: Systematic review of blockchain applications in healthcare examining benefits including transparency, security, and decentralization alongside implementation challenges
strengths: Systematic review methodology, comprehensive coverage of healthcare applications, balanced analysis of benefits and challenges
weaknesses: Limited to healthcare context, may not address research-specific requirements, implementation barriers may differ in research contexts
citation: AbdelSalam, Blockchain Revolutionizing Healthcare Industry: A Systematic Review, PHIM 2023

title: How Decentralized Science (DeSci) is Accelerating Scientific Research
authors: Token Metrics Research Team
hypotheses: DeSci represents an emerging investment narrative with potential for real-world impact while addressing systematic inefficiencies in traditional research funding
notes: Investment-focused analysis of DeSci ecosystem including BIO Protocol, VitaDAO, Molecule with market cap analysis and tokenomics evaluation
strengths: Market-focused perspective, comprehensive project analysis, quantitative metrics, practical investment insights
weaknesses: Investment-biased perspective, limited academic rigor, potential market volatility effects on analysis
citation: Token Metrics Research, How Decentralized Science (DeSci) is Accelerating Scientific Research, Token Metrics 2025

title: The 4 Steps to Get Your Research Funded by A DeSci DAO: A Step-by-Step Guide
authors: Jonathan Heppner
hypotheses: DeSci DAOs can provide alternative funding pathways for research areas traditionally underserved by conventional funding agencies
notes: Practical guide for researchers seeking DAO funding, highlighting non-conventional science areas like psychedelics, longevity, cryopreservation getting dedicated funding
strengths: Practical researcher focus, addresses real funding challenges, identifies underserved research areas, step-by-step implementation guide
weaknesses: Limited empirical validation, blog format rather than peer review, potential bias toward specific research areas
citation: Heppner, The 4 Steps to Get Your Research Funded by A DeSci DAO, ResearchHub Foundation 2024

title: Unlocking Scientific Innovation Through Decentralized Science – Part I
authors: Stanford Law School
hypotheses: DeSci represents application of blockchain's social change ideology to address institutional shortcomings in traditional centralized scientific systems
notes: Legal and institutional analysis of DeSci movement, examining blockchain's potential for creating transparent, secure scientific interactions without centralized authority
strengths: Institutional legal perspective, addresses systemic institutional challenges, comprehensive analysis of decentralization benefits
weaknesses: Limited technical implementation details, legal focus may not address practical deployment challenges, theoretical rather than empirical
citation: Stanford Law School, Unlocking Scientific Innovation Through Decentralized Science – Part I, Stanford Law 2023

title: DAOs (Decentralized Autonomous Organizations) in Scientific Research
authors: Dr. Adam Goulston
hypotheses: DAOs can reshape scientific research funding and coordination through blockchain-enabled governance systems that eliminate traditional hierarchies
notes: Analysis of VitaDAO case study funding $250K rapamycin aging study, examining DAO governance, smart contracts, and tokenized research contributions
strengths: Concrete case study with VitaDAO, practical implementation examples, addresses governance and token mechanics
weaknesses: Limited to single case study, early stage analysis, potential scalability and sustainability questions not fully addressed
citation: Goulston, DAOs (Decentralized Autonomous Organizations) in Scientific Research, MacroLingo 2024

title: Case Study: DeSci Labs and Filecoin: Enabling a Future of Open Science
authors: Filecoin Foundation
hypotheses: Decentralized storage infrastructure can address the scientific replication crisis by providing robust, accessible, and affordable tools for research reproducibility
notes: Case study of DeSci Labs using IPFS and Filecoin for scientific data storage and reproducibility. Addresses replication crisis with 70% of researchers failing to reproduce studies
strengths: Addresses fundamental reproducibility crisis, concrete technical implementation, real-world partnership example, infrastructure focus
weaknesses: Commercial case study with potential bias, limited peer review, focused on storage rather than broader research process
citation: Filecoin Foundation, Case Study: DeSci Labs and Filecoin: Enabling a Future of Open Science, Filecoin 2023

title: Floating Forests: Quantitative Validation of Citizen Science Data Generated From Consensus Classifications
authors: Isaac S. Rosenthal, Jarrett E. K. Byrnes, Kyle C. Cavanaugh, Tom W. Bell, Briana Harder, Alison J. Haupt, Andrew T. W. Rassweiler, Alejandro Pérez-Matus, Jorge Assis, Ali Swanson, Amy Boyer, Adam McMaster, Laura Trouille
hypotheses: Consensus-based citizen science classifications can generate quantitatively valid scientific data comparable to expert analysis when properly validated
notes: Floating Forests citizen science project validation study examining kelp forest mapping through crowdsourced satellite image analysis with quantitative validation methods
strengths: Rigorous quantitative validation, large-scale citizen science implementation, consensus-based approach, satellite data analysis
weaknesses: Limited to specific ecological domain, traditional validation against expert ground truth, no blockchain/decentralized aspects
citation: Rosenthal et al., Floating Forests: Quantitative Validation of Citizen Science Data Generated From Consensus Classifications, arXiv 2018

title: Empowering Government Efficiency Through Civic Intelligence
authors: Janne Ruponen
hypotheses: Civic intelligence platforms can enhance government efficiency through citizen participation in data collection and decision-making processes
notes: Examination of civic intelligence applications for government efficiency, exploring citizen participation in governance and public data collection
strengths: Government efficiency focus, citizen participation emphasis, practical governance applications, efficiency metrics
weaknesses: Limited to government context, may not directly apply to scientific research, traditional civic engagement approach
citation: Ruponen, Empowering Government Efficiency Through Civic Intelligence, Technologies 2024
